title: Comprehensive Placement and Routing Framework with Guaranteed In-Cell Routability for Synthesizing Complementary-FET Cells
problem: CFET cell layout synthesis faces extreme routing resource scarcity due to vertical transistor stacking; existing generators struggle with in-cell routability and produce suboptimal or infeasible layouts.
motivation: CFET is a critical technology scaling path beyond 5nm; enabling efficient cell generation accelerates technology adoption.
method: The approach works in three stages: first, it breaks transistors into smaller groups while keeping solution quality high, making the problem easier to solve; second, it places transistors using an SMT solver (a constraint-solving tool) that simultaneously checks whether connections can actually be routed, catching routing conflicts before they become expensive to fix; third, it routes the metal connections layer by layer—the bottom layer follows manual routing practices, while upper layers use integer linear programming (mathematical optimization) to handle the vertical stacking's unidirectional routing constraints.
key_novelty: The key advance is doing routability checks (verifying whether metal connections can fit) while placing transistors using a constraint solver, rather than after placement, which prevents layouts from becoming unroutable.
contributions: Partitioning strategy for large-scale CFET cells
SMT-based placement with embedded routability constraints
Progressive multi-layer routing with ILP optimization
Achieves smallest cell width and reduced metal usage vs SOTA generators

metrics.area: minimum cell width, reduced M2 usage

limitations: Framework specific to CFET; applicability to other advanced node technologies not discussed.
